capitals.name: Heijō-kyō (Nara)
capitals.note: 'Japan's capital is moved from Fujiwara-kyō to Heijō-kyō' (710).

capitals.name: Shigaraki-no-miya (Shigaraki)
capitals.note: 'Shigarakinomiya (紫香楽宮, present-day Shigaraki) in 745', then 'moved back to Nara in 745'.

capitals.name: Nagaoka-kyō (Nagaokakyō, Kyoto Prefecture)
capitals.note: 'the capital was moved in 784 to Nagaoka-kyō'; the page counts the Nagaoka decade in the Nara period.

keyframe_review.note: 230,061 km2, identical to the Asuka shape; no page opened gives an area. Verdict changed from ok to adjust (review jk-01-a): Asuka gained the Akita foothold in 709 ('In 709, the fort of Ideha was created close to present day Akita', Emishi page, re-read) and the Nara 710 shape does not hold it (gazetteer: 0 of the 21 cells of a 50 km circle at Akita lie inside it). No loss is recorded: the Emishi page describes none for 710-794, and the Akita Castle page says 'In 733, the fort on the Mogami River was moved north' and that the court 'decided to abolish the Akita Castle in 770 but withdrew the decision ten years later' (it dates the creation of Dewa Country to 708 and the fort's abandonment to c. 1050), so the foothold is kept in the shape and in the found event. The ledger's 724 (Taga Fort 'near present-day Sendai') and 758 ('northern Miyagi', Momonofu) gains carry the frontier from the shape's 38.2 N limit to the Kitakami; Tsushima outside the bbox is noted, not corrected (page budget).

correction.text: the Nara 710 shape plus the Ideha (Dewa) foothold near Akita that the Asuka court gained in 709 and that no page records lost; the northern limit is the 724 and 758 gains of the ledger
the Nara 788 shape unchanged, plus the Akita foothold (Ideha, 709; Akita Castle moved north 733 and kept in 770); holds 788 to 794, when the court moves to Heian-kyō

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria ends the row in 792 and starts Heian Japan in 793; the page runs the Nara period 'from 710 to 794'. The 788 break is unexplained (identical area). The Akita foothold of the 710 keyframe is carried here (review jk-01-a).

region.text: the realm ruled from Heijō-kyō, with the Ideha foothold near Akita gained in 709

ledger.note: 710: the capital moves to Heijō-kyō (Nara). 'Japan's capital is moved from Fujiwara-kyō to Heijō-kyō'; the period 'covers the years from 710 to 794'. The Akita foothold gained by the Asuka court in 709 ('the fort of Ideha was created close to present day Akita', Emishi page) is part of the realm; no page records its loss.

region.text: 'Taga Fort was built by Ōno no Omi Azumahito near present-day Sendai'

ledger.note: 724: Taga Castle founded on the Sendai plain. 'In 724 Taga Fort was built by Ōno no Omi Azumahito near present-day Sendai'; he 'steadily built forts across the Sendai plain and into the interior mountains'; Taga became 'the largest administrative fort in the northeast region of Michinoku' (Thirty-Eight Years' War page).
740: the court moves to Kuni-kyō. 'to Kuni-kyō (present-day Kizugawa) in 740–744'.
744: the court moves to Naniwa-kyō. 'to Naniwa-kyō (present-day Osaka) in 744–745'.
745: the court at Shigaraki. 'Shigarakinomiya (present-day Shigaraki) in 745'.
745: the court returns to Heijō-kyō. 'moved back to Nara in 745'.

region.text: 'what is now northern Miyagi Prefecture'; Momonofu Castle on the Kitakami River

ledger.note: 758: Momonofu Castle on the Kitakami. Fujiwara no Asakari's army 'penetrated into what is now northern Miyagi Prefecture' and built Momonofu Castle on the Kitakami River (758).

region.text: the Sendai plain and the Kitakami valley forts (Monou, Taga, Momonofu), where 'the Emishi stormed Monou castle and the rebellion began'

ledger.note: 774: the Thirty-Eight Years' War begins. 'On 5 September, 774 CE, the Emishi stormed Monou castle and the rebellion began'; in 776 'a huge army of over 20,000 men was sent to attack the Shiwa Emishi, an effort that failed'; in 780 the Emishi 'attacked the Sendai plain, torching Japanese villages there'; in 789 Ki no Kosami 'was defeated by the Isawa Emishi under their general Aterui' at the Koromo River and 'lost a thousand men'.
784: the court moves to Nagaoka-kyō. 'the capital was moved in 784 to Nagaoka-kyō'.

region.text: the Sendai plain and the Kitakami valley forts (Monou, Taga, Momonofu), where 'the Emishi stormed Monou castle and the rebellion began'

ledger.note: 794: the war passes to the Heian dossier. The fighting ran to 811 ('it was not until 811 that the so-called Thirty-Eight Years' War was over'); this end marks only the change of dossier when the court moved to Heian-kyō; in 794 'many key Shiwa Emishi, including Isawa no kimi Anushiko, became allies of the Japanese'.

region.text: the whole realm, with the Akita foothold and the Miyagi frontier forts (Taga 724, Momonofu 758), passes to the court at Heian-kyō

ledger.note: 794: the court moves to Heian-kyō; the Nara period ends. 'and in 794 to Heian-kyō'.

wars.name: Fujiwara no Hirotsugu rebellion
wars.outcome: 'In 740, a member of the Fujiwara clan, Hirotsugu, launched a rebellion from his base in Fukuoka, Kyushu'; the page gives no outcome sentence; no border moved.

wars.name: Fujiwara no Nakamaro rebellion
wars.outcome: 'Nakamaro rose up in arms in 764 but was quickly crushed.'

wars.name: Thirty-Eight Years' War

zones.text: the Sendai plain and the Kitakami valley forts (Monou, Taga, Momonofu), where 'the Emishi stormed Monou castle and the rebellion began'

wars.outcome: The Nara court held the Sendai plain and lost Monou (774); the war continued under the Heian court until 'Aterui's surrender in 802' and the end in 811 (Heian dossier).
wars.note: Infobox dates '774–812'; Result and Territorial fields blank on the page. Monou stormed 5 September 774; the 776 campaign against the Shiwa Emishi failed; 780 raids on the Sendai plain; 789 defeat at the Koromo River. The war ran 774-811; years clipped to this dossier's life (reviewer jk-01-a), the Heian dossier carries 794-811.

certainty.note: The northern frontier is a line of stockades on the Sendai plain and the Japan Sea coast ('the territory between Akita and the northwest was not under government control'); the Hayato south and the islands are not on the pages opened.

notes: Cliopatria 710-792 against the page's 710-794: the 788 shape is extended to 794 and Heian Japan starts in 794 (one-year overlap convention). Counterpart 'emishi' for the frontier gains and the Thirty-Eight Years' War, as in the Asuka and Heian dossiers; no row covers the Emishi. Not on the pages opened: the Hayato rebellion (720), Dewa Province (712), Akita Castle (733), Tanegashima, Yakushima and Amami tribute, the planned Silla expedition (759-764), the Taga Castle burning of 780 by Korehari no Azamaro (the page says only that 'Even Taga Castle was not spared'). Tsushima lies outside the bbox of both shapes; see the Heian dossier. Review fix (jk-01-a-fixed): the Akita foothold gained in 709 (Asuka ledger) is now in the 710 and 788 keyframes, the found and dissolve regions and the predecessor and successor land; Dewa Province was created in 708 on the Akita Castle page (not 712), Akita Castle was moved north in 733, so the thin item 'Dewa 712, Akita Castle 733' is partly answered; the Hayato rebellion (720) is still not on any page opened. The 794 contest_end (ledger) stays confidence 1: a technical handover of the Thirty-Eight Years' War to the Heian dossier, no page needed. The Asuka dossier (verdict pass) was not touched: its dissolve region and successor land still name the 705 shape only.
